text:
maria: seeing a stair-stepped latency increase from a subset of inference pods in us-west2 starting ~1779001210. spikes correlate with instance terminations in mixed-capacity pool :thinking_face:
raj: confirmed, metrics show token latency p95 climbed from 120ms -> 900ms for model shard group b. CPU on nodes looks fine but GPU attach/detach logs show churn.
sophie: I pulled node events: a burst of spot preemptions + two AZ rebalancing actions within 45s. looks like auction surge.
maria: here’s excerpt from kube events:
```
Warning  NodeTerminated  45s (x3 over 1m)  kubelet  Node was preempted by provider: TERMINATE_INSTANCE
Normal   NodeReady       30s              kubelet  Node became ready
```
raj: infra-bot reports provider-side NACKs during allocation window — capacity throttle. that caused scheduler to remap pods between on-demand and spot which amplified KV cache misses.
leo: consequence: cache miss + model cold-start on fallback nodes -> big token latency. also saw a few OOM kills on model-side container after failed warmup.
sophie: mitigation options: 1) temporarily widen dedicated pool + scale-up reserved nodes in us-west2, 2) pin critical routes to on-demand only, 3) reduce batchSize / force async fallback for affected routes.
maria: I already pushed a small routing config change to prefer dedicated for route `/v1/generate/low-latency` with 5s rollout. deploy-bot: rollout started 1779001252 :rocket:
raj: starting a rapid scale request to infra API to add 6 reserved GPUs to the dedicated pool (eta ~3m). if that lands, we can move warm models there and drain churny nodes.
leo: cost question — adding 6 reserved GPUs for an hour is ~ $48 (rough), but avoids customer P95 SLO violations. recommend approve.
sophie: @maria please also add a cache-warmup job to the plan: replicate KV prefixes for the two most-used model keys to dedicated nodes once they join.
maria: on it. will run warmup script after nodes become ready: `./scripts/warmup_kv.sh --model shard-b --targets tag:dedicated-us-west2`
raj: infra API returned success, reserved nodes provisioning started 1779001268. monitoring nodes join.
infra-bot: 1779001279 nodes-added: 6 reserved-GPUs in pool 'dedicated-us-west2' (ids: r-4521..r-4526)
maria: warmup kicked, initial latency p95 dropping to ~200ms for the route.
leo: rolling drain on suspect spot nodes to reduce churn. draining pods will trigger re-schedules to dedicated pool.
sophie: after drain finishes we'll leave a temporary policy: prefer-dedicated for latency-critical models for next 2 hours, then re-evaluate. logging retention increased for scheduling traces.
raj: postmortem action items: - add early warning when spot termination rate > 10% in 1m - auto-evict low-priority jobs before model rehomes - simulate mixed-pool churn in chaos env.
maria: agreed. for now customers restored, continuing to monitor for 30m. thanks team :thumbsup:
leo: heads-up for cost team: will post an incident note with estimated incremental cost ~ $60 for the hour (includes warmup and reserve overhead).
sophie: closing loop — I’ll own the post-incident RFC for making dedicated fallback opt-in per-route.
maria: marking thread resolved in 1779001289.
